title: Keep original request through chained retries; answer study review 1
summary: Fix `earlier_attempt` so "try again on <job>", where that job was itself a retry, carries the original request and not just the "try again on …" line. Then answer the 7 majors, minors and nits of the study capability M1 design review 1 in a written response and a design revision, using the review's own finding ids.

defaults_applied.how: The retry-of-a-retry fix gets a failing-first test; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check must pass.
Two focused pieces only: the retry fix and the review response. No new capability work.
The response and the design revisions are written for an outside reader, with finding ids cited.
Each response cites the review finding and the design section it changed; any new numbers are labeled estimates.
"Review 1" was resolved from the repository: the study M1 design status line and CHANGELOG say its findings are unanswered.
The fix is Rust; the docs are Markdown, which the repository already uses.
Retry behavior is verified by running the lifecycle test.

assumptions: "review 1" means the study capability M1 design review (docs/design/reviews/study-capability-m1-review-1.md), the only review the repository records as unanswered. The design's status line says so. The athena-v0 review 1 is answered in design Appendix D.
"Answered" means a written response to every finding plus the matching design revisions, in the style of athena-v0.md Appendix D. It does not mean building the capability.

The 8 decisions for the user cannot be settled by the producer. It proposes defaults, marks them as pending the user, and takes the more conservative option (for example, non-waivable evidence rules, containment named, structural checks).

The retry bug is: when the rejected job's request is itself "try again on X", the brief's Earlier attempt carries that retry line, not the original request. The fix follows the chain back to the first non-retry request and keeps each job's findings. The retried job's own request stays as typed.
The user's local, uncommitted state does not matter; this is one commit with the fix first and the doc response second.

acceptance_criteria.text: Retrying a retry: after job A is rejected, job B ("try again on A") is rejected, and job C is asked "try again on B", C's reader brief has an "Earlier attempt" section containing A's original request text. B's findings still appear. Check with a new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs; run `cargo test`.
A single retry ("try again on A" where A is not itself a retry) produces the same brief as before, and the existing retry tests still pass; run `cargo test`.
Retry errors are unchanged: an unknown job, a job that is not rejected, and a bare "try again on" are each still refused with an error naming the job. Run `cargo test`.
Everything carried from the chain, including the original request, goes through the redactor; a test or existing test shows this. Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy`, and `cargo fmt --check`; all clean.
Following the chain of retries cannot loop forever or panic. Its depth is bounded or it tracks visited ids, and the code comment says which.

Each of the review's 17 findings (M1–M7, m1–m8, n1–n2) has a response naming the finding id and saying what changed in the design or why it did not. This is in a response section or file linked from the design.

The design's status line no longer says "findings not yet answered". It links the response, and says whether a re-check of the revised design is still required by §9 before any build job. The response lists the 8 "Decisions for the user", each with a proposed answer marked as awaiting the user.

The design revision makes the changes the review asks for in the sections it names (e.g. evidence rules non-waivable, the `sha` field on `study.run/1`, a rule for `both`, the `quote` and `contradicts` fields, redaction and containment), or records a reasoned deferral. No code, crate, or config is added for the study capability.
CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] records the retry fix and the review response. No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, Cargo lint tables) is changed.

out_of_scope: Building the athena-cap-study crate or any study code
Running a second independent review of the revised design
Changing how the new job's own request is stored or typed
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows, or lint configuration
Edits to BRIEF.md or the athena-v0 design and its reviews, other than the study review's header if a link is needed
departures: Cost and time are above the reference because the request bundles a code fix with a design response to 17 findings, including 7 majors, over a long design document. The verifier must also check each finding was answered. Acceptance and verification odds are lower because "get review 1 answered" is loosely defined and the 8 user decisions are open.
